scenes.headline: How one ownership rule runs Bend 2
scenes.sub: Behind the type theory, the proof kernel and a runtime with no collector.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Nacho! Bend 2 is a language that checks proofs and runs on GPUs. One small rule does most of the work.

scenes.label: The rule
scenes.text: A value has exactly one owner unless its type says it's Data. That one rule makes the logic consistent, removes the garbage collector, and reshaped the runtime.
scenes.say: A value has exactly one owner, unless its type says it's Data. That one rule makes the logic consistent, removes the garbage collector, and reshaped the runtime.

scenes.title: Laws, proofs, and one small kernel

steps.say: A human writes the laws a program must obey. An AI writes the code and the proofs, which are ordinary functions.

steps.note: a check proves code matches the law, not that the law is right
steps.say: One small, human-audited kernel checks them. The file either checks, or it doesn't compile.
Then a mostly AI-written compiler, not yet audited, emits C, Metal, CUDA or JavaScript. That link is tested, not proven.

scenes.title: Why Type in Type stays consistent

left.title: The usual fix
items: A hierarchy of universes blocks it
left.say: Letting Type have type Type usually invites a classic paradox. Most systems add a hierarchy of universes.

right.title: BendTT's fix: affinity
items: Every known paradox copies a function
Functions are never Data, so they can't be copied
right.say: Bend blocks it differently. Every known paradox copies a function, and functions are never Data, so the checker refuses the copy.

items.say: The new runtime dropped interaction nets. It reference-counts only the types that are actually shared.

items.text: Everything else: plain stores and frees
items.say: Everything else compiles to plain loads, stores and frees. No garbage collector.

items.text: Fork with a let, bang for GPU
items.say: Parallelism is explicit: a two-name let forks two calls, and a bang sends a call to the GPU.

scenes.title: Game of life, in seconds
scenes.note: one core: 0.8 to 1.5x of C, but hashmap runs 4.4x slower
scenes.say: Against a hand-written C twin, one core is close: seven point eight seconds to six point seven eight. The GPU is far faster.

scenes.text: Affinity does triple duty: it keeps the logic consistent, removes the collector, and trades automatic parallelism for predictable speed.

recap: Laws, proofs, and one small audited kernel
No copied functions, so no paradox
Ownership, not interaction nets, at runtime
scenes.say: To recap: a small kernel checks your laws, affinity keeps the logic sound, and ownership replaced interaction nets.
